checklist_item.title: Verify Consensus Layer correctly obtains active validator indices for epoch-based proposer selection

reachability.notes: If inactive validators are included in the selection pool, they could be chosen as proposers but would be unable to produce blocks.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Review the get_active_validator_indices function implementation. 2. Verify it correctly checks validator activation_epoch <= epoch < exit_epoch. 3. Confirm slashed validators are excluded from the active set if required by spec. 4. Test edge cases: validators activating at current epoch, validators exiting at current epoch, validators with pending withdrawals. 5. Verify the epoch parameter is correctly passed from get_beacon_proposer_indices to get_active_validator_indices.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-38, Supporting node check for actor-consensus-layer. Ensures the active validator filtering logic is correct.

checklist_item.title: Verify Validator actor cannot influence proposer selection to include inactive validators

reachability.notes: If inactive validators are included in the selection pool, they could be chosen as proposers but would be unable to produce blocks.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Identify any validator-controlled inputs that flow into proposer selection logic. 2. Verify that validator attestations or block proposals cannot manipulate the active validator set used for proposer indices. 3. Check that state transitions updating validator status (activation, exit, slashing) correctly reflect in subsequent proposer computations. 4. Ensure no race conditions exist between validator status updates and proposer index calculations.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-38, Supporting node check for actor-validator. Ensures validators cannot manipulate proposer selection.

checklist_item.title: Can IGNORED sidecars be permanently discarded or forwarded without re-validation?

reachability.notes: Incorrect IGNORE handling could cause data loss (permanent discard) or amplification (forwarding).

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Identify the gossip validation handler for blob sidecars (p2p-SG-006). 2. Trace all code paths where IGNORE is returned as the validation result. 3. For each IGNORE path, verify that the sidecar is queued for later re-processing (not discarded). 4. Verify that IGNORED sidecars are NOT forwarded to other peers. 5. Attempt to trigger IGNORE conditions (e.g., sidecar arrives before its parent block) and confirm the sidecar is retained in a pending queue. 6. Verify the queue has proper bounds and eviction policies to prevent memory exhaustion. 7. Confirm that queued sidecars are re-validated when their dependencies become available.
checklist_item.falsification_strategy: Design a test that triggers an IGNORE condition and then verifies: (a) the sidecar is not permanently discarded by checking it remains accessible for later processing, and (b) the sidecar is not forwarded by monitoring outbound P2P messages. A successful violation would show either data loss (sidecar unavailable when needed) or message amplification (IGNORED sidecar propagated).
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-23, Invariant: p2p-SG-006-INV-002, Assumption: asm-007. Bug bounty requires PoC showing IGNORED sidecar being forwarded without re-validation.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is proposer selection seed correctly domain-separated using DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER?

reachability.notes: Incorrect domain would cause proposer selection to correlate with attestation committee selection or sync committee selection, reducing unpredictability.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate the proposer selection implementation that uses get_seed(). 2. Verify that get_seed() is called with exactly three arguments: state, epoch, and DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER. 3. Check that DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER is a distinct constant from other domain constants (DOMAIN_BEACON_ATTESTER, DOMAIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE, etc.). 4. Trace all call sites of get_seed() for proposer selection and confirm no alternative domain values are used. 5. Verify that no code paths exist where proposer selection bypasses domain-separated seed generation. 6. Test that changing the domain constant produces different proposer selections for the same epoch/state.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-39, Source Invariant: FULU-SG006-INV-002, Threat: stride-017, Trust Boundary: tb-009. Wrong domain separation would make proposer selection predictable or correlated with other selections, enabling MEV extraction and potential consensus manipulation.

checklist_item.title: Verify Domain Constant Uniqueness: Are all domain separation constants (DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER, DOMAIN_BEACON_ATTESTER, etc.) guaranteed to be unique?

reachability.notes: Incorrect domain would cause proposer selection to correlate with attestation committee selection or sync committee selection, reducing unpredictability.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Enumerate all DOMAIN_* constants used in the codebase. 2. Verify each domain constant has a unique value that cannot collide with others. 3. Check that domain constants are defined as immutable/constant values. 4. Verify no dynamic computation or user input can influence domain values. 5. Confirm domain constants match the Ethereum consensus specification exactly.
checklist_item.notes: Supporting check for boundary edge tb-009. Domain collision would break the security guarantees of randomness separation.

checklist_item.title: Can process_epoch sub-process execution order be violated, causing state divergence across clients?

reachability.notes: Reordering epoch processing steps would cause different state after epoch transitions, leading to consensus failures. The proposer lookahead must be last because it depends on the updated validator set.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Identify all 16 epoch sub-processes within process_epoch (including EIP-7917's process_proposer_lookahead as the 16th step). 2. Map the dependency graph between sub-processes to understand which state mutations each step relies upon. 3. Verify that no code path allows sub-processes to execute out of order. 4. Create a test harness that artificially reorders sub-process execution and compare resulting beacon state hashes against correctly-ordered execution. 5. Specifically verify that process_proposer_lookahead executes AFTER all 15 prior steps complete. 6. Check for any race conditions or concurrent access patterns. 7. Validate that state mutations from each step are properly committed before the next step begins.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-40, Invariant: FULU-SG007-INV-001, Assumption: asm-014.

checklist_item.title: Can process_proposer_lookahead execute before all 15 preceding steps in process_epoch complete?

reachability.notes: If process_proposer_lookahead runs before validator registry updates, it would compute the lookahead using stale validator data.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Identify the process_epoch function and verify it contains exactly 16 ordered steps. 2. Confirm process_proposer_lookahead is invoked as step 16 (the final step). 3. Trace data dependencies: verify process_proposer_lookahead reads from validator registry, randao mix, and other state that is modified by steps 1-15. 4. Attempt to invoke process_proposer_lookahead with pre-update state. 5. Check for any code paths (error handling, early returns, conditional branches) that could cause process_proposer_lookahead to execute before steps 1-15 complete.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-41, Invariant: FULU-SG007-INV-002, Assumption: asm-014.

reachability.notes: An off-by-one in the shift amount would leave stale entries at the front or remove entries for the current epoch, causing proposer assignment errors.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate the process_proposer_lookahead function implementation. 2. Verify the shift operation uses exactly SLOTS_PER_EPOCH as the offset. 3. Trace the array slice operation. 4. Create test cases with boundary values. 5. Verify that after shift, the first entry corresponds to the correct epoch's first slot proposer.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-42, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Invariant: FULU-SG008-INV-001.

checklist_item.title: Verify Consensus Layer proposer_lookahead state consistency during epoch transitions

reachability.notes: An off-by-one in the shift amount would leave stale entries at the front or remove entries for the current epoch, causing proposer assignment errors.

checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-42, Covered Node: actor-validator. Supporting check for boundary integrity.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is the sidecar subnet validation correctly enforced in the gossip validation pipeline?
checklist_item.test_procedure:
1. Identify the gossip validation handler for data column sidecars in the P2P layer.
2. Locate the implementation of compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(sidecar.index) and verify it is called during validation.
3. Craft a test sidecar with index=5 and attempt to publish it on subnet_id=0 (incorrect subnet).
4. Verify that the sidecar is REJECTED with an appropriate error indicating subnet mismatch.
5. Repeat with various index/subnet combinations to ensure all mismatches are rejected.
6. Verify that a correctly matched sidecar (index=5 on subnet_id=5) is accepted.
7. Check that no cross-subnet pollution occurs by monitoring subnet message queues.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-29, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Threat: stride-024

checklist_item.title: Does the P2P peer correctly reject sidecars with mismatched subnet/index before forwarding to the beacon node?
checklist_item.test_procedure:
1. Trace the message flow from P2P peer reception to beacon node processing.
2. Verify that subnet validation occurs at the P2P layer BEFORE any message is passed to the beacon node.
3. Inject a malformed sidecar (index=3 on subnet_id=7) at the P2P peer layer.
4. Confirm the message is dropped at the P2P layer and never reaches the beacon node.
5. Check logs/metrics to verify rejection is recorded with the correct reason code.
6. Verify no partial processing or state changes occur in the beacon node for rejected sidecars.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-29, Node: actor-p2p-peer, Trust Boundary: tb-001

checklist_item.title: Does the beacon node have defense-in-depth validation for sidecar subnet matching as a secondary check?
checklist_item.test_procedure:
1. Review the beacon node's sidecar processing code for any secondary subnet validation.
2. If secondary validation exists, verify it uses the same compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar function.
3. Simulate a scenario where P2P validation is bypassed (e.g., direct internal call) with a mismatched sidecar.
4. Verify the beacon node rejects or handles the invalid sidecar gracefully.
5. If no secondary validation exists, document this as a defense-in-depth gap.
6. Verify that accepted sidecars are stored/processed with correct subnet associations.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-29, Node: actor-beacon-node, Supporting check for defense-in-depth

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does the gossip validation pipeline correctly IGNORE (not REJECT) sidecars with future slots?
checklist_item.test_procedure:
1. Identify the gossip validation handler for blob sidecars in the P2P layer.
2. Review the validation logic that checks block_header.slot against current_slot.
3. Verify that sidecars with block_header.slot > current_slot return IGNORE status, not REJECT.
4. Confirm that IGNORE responses do not trigger peer penalties or scoring decrements.
5. Test by sending sidecars with slots 1, 10, 100, and MAX_UINT64 slots in the future and verify consistent IGNORE behavior.
6. Check that IGNORED sidecars are not permanently discarded but can be re-validated after clock advancement.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-30, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Primary Element: p2p:SG-006:q_check_future_slot.

checklist_item.title: Is the P2P peer handling of future-slot sidecars resilient to resource exhaustion attacks?
checklist_item.test_procedure:
1. Locate the queue or buffer that stores IGNORED future-slot sidecars in the actor-p2p-peer component.
2. Determine if there is a bounded size limit on this queue.
3. Send a flood of far-future-slot sidecars from a malicious peer and monitor memory consumption.
4. Verify that the queue has appropriate eviction policies.
5. Check that excessive IGNORE entries do not cause memory exhaustion or degrade node performance.
6. Confirm that legitimate future-slot sidecars are not evicted by attacker-controlled far-future entries.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-30, Node: actor-p2p-peer.

checklist_item.title: Does the beacon node correctly re-validate previously IGNORED future-slot sidecars after clock advancement?
checklist_item.test_procedure:
1. Locate the re-validation mechanism in the actor-beacon-node component that processes previously IGNORED sidecars.
2. Verify that when current_slot advances, sidecars with block_header.slot <= new_current_slot are re-evaluated.
3. Test by sending a sidecar for slot N+1 when current slot is N, then advance the clock to slot N+1.
4. Confirm the previously IGNORED sidecar is now accepted and processed correctly.
5. Check for race conditions between clock advancement and sidecar re-validation.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-30, Node: actor-beacon-node.

5. Verify the sidecar is REJECTED.
6. Test edge case where sidecar.slot == parent.slot + 1 to confirm valid sidecars are accepted.
7. Test edge case where sidecar.slot < parent.slot to confirm rejection.
